name: purchase coverage reads the claim's normalised counterparty; a purchase with no counterparty is never covered
notes: §6.1 (v1.2) coverage 'none': a purchase-like type (sources ['gmail.receipt']) whose normalised counterparty (name(), §11) is not in policy.receiptMerchants, or which has no counterparty, has coverage none. receiptMerchants is patched to ['acme']; one gmail.receipt entry (acct-a) saw [09:00, 15:00] and synced 15:00.

c1 'ACME' 3000 USD (10:02) × o1 merchant 'Acme' 3000 USD (10:02): name('ACME') = 'acme' ∈ receiptMerchants, so coverage comes from the intervals: [10:00, 10:48] ⊆ [09:00, 15:00] → full. Applicable: timeProximity 2500, amountExact 2500, merchantMatch 2000 (no subject); Σw = 7000. tp 1; amountExact 1 (3000 USD both); merchantMatch 1 (normalised 'acme' = 'acme') → S = 7000/7000 = 1/1 → verified, FINAL (15:00 ≥ end + 30 = 10:33). Comparing the raw 'ACME' with the list instead would make it no_coverage.

c2 3000 USD with no counterparty (12:02): identity amountExact is applicable → not underspecified, and the claim is assignable, but nothing is in its window [12:00, 12:48] → match.none. Coverage is none although the receipt interval contains the window (no parser can be known to have seen it) → rule no_coverage, reason coverage.none {source: gmail.receipt}. PENDING (§8): 15:00 < end + finalizeUnverifiableHours = 10-07 12:03. Reading the interval alone would give full coverage, graceElapsed (15:00 ≥ 12:48) → a false NOT_FOUND.
o1 is outside c2's window. No activity → no orphan receipts.
